newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Monday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were narrowly mixed but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.48/1.43 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 1.45/1.40 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.56/1.51 percent against 1.58/1.53 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.62/99.67 from last Friday's close of S$99.61/99.71, September 2001 at S$96.92/96.97 versus S$96.90/96.95 and June 2003 at S$94.96/95.01 against S$94.92/94.97.
The interbank rate rose slightly to 3-13/16 3-11/16 percent from last Friday's 3-9/16 3-7/16 percent.
